title: Goldkette arrangements, the NEA grant and the Disney World offer
summary: He reconstructed the Goldkette arrangements from records, applied for an NEA grant, and refused to perform them with little rehearsal at Disney World.

blocks.x: Yeah, right after that.
You were telling me, it didn't go through because
Right.
-- you wanted to do it.
In the meantime I had been working on these things, because I wanted to do them.
The Goldkette thing.

And he called me when I had a lot of them finished. I had tried to get these and put them all together, so that would have been before the guitar. Because I wanted to try to interest somebody in making it for a band. That stuff is hard to get out.
I had to get the records and take them off the record, which is very tedious.
So what did you do for the National Endowment?
Well, I did that.
And it was recorded.
No. They were waiting for me to record it.
Did you do a concert?
I didn't do a concert.
You just did the --
I just did the material and applied for it. My brother got me to apply for that. He dug up the
books and dug up the NEA material and application form for it and so forth.
So where does it stand now.
They want to do it down in Walt Disney place down in Florida.
Disneyworld.

Yes. I don't want to do it that way. You get down there and they give you about four days rehearsal. Similar to Wein's and you know, all you need is a substitute, and you can throw the whole thing right off. I don't want -- especially out of town, although a guy like Joe has been very nice. He wanted me to go to Europe and do it.
